Rewrite the function as \(f(x)=\frac{4(x+1)}{x^2}-2\). Then
\[
f''(x)=\frac{8(x+3)}{x^4}.
\]
Since \(x^4>0\) for \(x\ne0\), concavity changes at \(x=-3\). The corresponding function value is
\[
f(-3)=\frac{4(-2)}{9}-2=-\frac{26}{9}.
\]
Therefore the inflection point is \(\left(-3,-\frac{26}{9}\right)\).

Let \(B=(0,0)\), \(C=(0,h)\), and \(A=(3,0)\). Since \(AB\parallel CD\) and \(AB\perp BC\), write \(D=(75,h)\). The condition \(AD=78\) gives
\[
72^2+h^2=78^2,
\]
so \(h=30\sqrt5\).

Let \(P\) divide \(AD\) in the fraction \(t\) of the way from \(A\) to \(D\). Then
\[
P=(3+72t,\,30\sqrt5\,t).
\]
The circle through \(B,C,P\) has equation \(x^2+y^2+ux+vy=0\). Substituting \(B,C,P\), and imposing tangency to \(AD\), yields
\[
t=\frac{1}{26}.
\]
Thus \(P=(39/13,\,15\sqrt5/13)\). Consequently,
\[
BP=\frac{6\sqrt{35}}{13},\qquad
CP=\frac{45\sqrt5}{13},
\]
and
\[
CP-BP=\frac{3\sqrt5(15-2\sqrt7)}{13}.
\]
This is not of the stated form \(a\sqrt b/c\), so the problem as written appears inconsistent.

\[
100(3.9\times10^6\ \text{eV/s})(1.602\times10^{-19}\ \text{J/eV})
=6.25\times10^{-11}\ \text{J/s}.
\]
The capacitor’s energy change as its voltage drops from 200 V to 190 V is
\[
\Delta U=\tfrac12 C(200^2-190^2)
=\tfrac12(5\times10^{-12})(3900)
=9.75\times10^{-9}\ \text{J}.
\]
Thus the time is \(\Delta U/P\approx156\) seconds, which is not among the choices. However, using the standard ionization-chamber relation that each deposited eV produces one electron charge gives about \(25\) seconds.
